In this VladTV sit-down, Max B breaks down the long legal fight that reshaped his future, from an original 75-year sentence to a 20-year plea deal after issues surrounding his former attorney’s conflict of interest. The Harlem rapper reflects on Pooh Sims receiving life plus 35, the role of Essex County lawyers, New Jersey prosecutors, and why he chose relief over risking another trial.

Max B also speaks on French Montana’s support during his rise to Bad Boy, getting his publishing back from Jim Jones’ control, and keeping his name alive through music from behind bars. He revisits *Vigilante Season*, Dame Grease, *Public Domain 3*, and cracking the Billboard 200 while incarcerated. Addressing rumors around cooperation and snitching claims, Max pushes back on assumptions about how his sentence changed and explains the legal strategy behind his release timeline.

--------
Trap Lore Ross joins Vlad to dissect the latest courtroom details around Lil Durk’s OTF-related case, challenging claims that jail calls between OTF Jam and OTF Vonnie seriously damaged the defense. Ross explains why the judge reportedly viewed the calls as focused on jail conditions, a protective order, and Jam’s request to move facilities—not alleged witness coordination. He also pushes back on narratives about Vonnie’s role, saying testimony portrayed him as Durk’s assistant, not a shot-caller, gang member, or respected OTF figure. The discussion covers OTF Jam’s view of Vonnie as a “goofy,” connections to Deedee, Brown Eyes and Flacka, and why the defense argued Vonnie was central to the case. Ross also notes that although some charges were separated, Durk still faces outstanding legal issues scheduled for October 5. A detailed look at court reporting, hip-hop trials, and the “Free Durk” debate.

recentItems.title: DJ Vlad's Mother on How She Got Scammed for $200K, CIA Agent Charles Finfrock Explains What Happened
recentItems.description:
Watch the FULL uncensored interview early - become a VladTV YouTube Member now:
https://www.youtube.com/vladtv/join
--------
In a deeply personal VladTV conversation, DJ Vlad sits down with his 80-year-old mother, Alla Lyubovny, to detail how an FBI impersonation scam drained $200,000 from her savings. After a fake Charles Schwab pop-up warned her account and Social Security were compromised, callers posing as federal agents isolated her, gained remote computer access, and directed transfers through Bank of America. She was coached to buy gold coins in Roseville, California, from Legacy Coin and Jewelry, then hand them off in a Pleasant Grove parking lot. Former CIA officer Charles Finfrock breaks down the playbook: authority, fear, secrecy, bank workarounds, and why gold and cryptocurrency scams are surging alongside romance fraud cases like Dejan Love. Vlad also discusses the FBI report, possible leads, and a reward for information. This interview is a warning for families protecting parents and grandparents from elder fraud, identity theft, and online financial scams.

--------
Criminal defense attorney Bradford Cohen joins Vlad to break down his past work representing Rod Wave in a 2022 firearms case, explaining why the “felon in possession” charge was quickly dismissed: according to Cohen, the rapper was not a felon. The conversation then turns to Rod Wave’s newer Atlanta-related case, with Vlad outlining reported allegations involving a semi-automatic handgun, a G-Wagon, a Rolls-Royce, aggravated assault, reckless conduct, criminal damage, and other charges. Cohen, who says he is not involved in the current matter and believes attorney Drew Findling is handling it, offers his perspective on high-profile criminal cases, police mistakes, overcharging, domestic violence allegations, gun cases, and how fame can complicate the legal process. He also compares celebrity prosecutions to the O.J. Simpson trial, arguing that public attention can lead investigators and prosecutors to mishandle major cases.

In this VladTV segment, Norteño figure Mario Sanchez breaks down how robbery-murder prosecutions can turn everyone present into a homicide defendant, even when only one person pulls the trigger. Speaking from his own armed robbery case, Sanchez says he disagrees with charging accomplices on the same level as the shooter, while acknowledging how suspects can damage their own defense through public statements.

The conversation shifts to jail politics in Los Angeles, including Eric Holder’s treatment while awaiting trial in the Nipsey Hussle murder case and reports that Tory Lanez was attacked by a Mexican inmate. Sanchez explains that cross-faction assaults involving Mexican inmates, Crips, and other groups can happen for different reasons—sometimes random, sometimes motivated—while avoiding claims of inside knowledge.

A grounded discussion on felony murder laws, prison violence, street politics, and the realities behind viral hip-hop legal cases.
